details.question: PostgreSQL 官方文档中，`synchronous_commit=remote_apply` 会让 COMMIT 等待到什么状态？这对只读查询的可见性意味着什么？
details.reference_answer: `remote_apply` 会让每次提交等待当前同步备库确认已经重放该事务；因此事务随后对备库上的用户查询可见。
details.model_answer:
When `synchronous_commit=remote_apply` is set, a `COMMIT` will wait for the synchronous standby to acknowledge that the transaction has been applied (i.e., the data is visible on the standby). If the primary receives a cancellation signal (e.g., `CTRL+C` or a client abort), PostgreSQL will still report success locally but will issue a warning: [S2](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/cac4b9df-92c6-77aa-687b-18b86cb13728@stratox.cz)
> "WARNING: canceling wait for synchronous replication due to user request [S2](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/cac4b9df-92c6-77aa-687b-18b86cb13728@stratox.cz)
> DETAIL: The transaction has already committed locally, but might not have been replicated to the standby." [S2](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/cac4b9df-92c6-77aa-687b-18b86cb13728@stratox.cz)
This means the transaction is committed on the primary, but the standby may not yet have received or applied it. [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
**Implications for read-only queries:** [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
Because the transaction is considered committed on the primary, read-only queries on the primary will see the new data. However, if the primary fails and a standby is promoted, the standby may not have received the transaction (if the cancellation occurred before the standby acknowledged it). In that case, the promoted standby will not contain the transaction, and read-only queries on the new primary will not see the data. Thus, the transaction is not guaranteed to be visible to all readers in a failover scenario. [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)

details.question: PostgreSQL 官方文档中，`synchronous_commit=remote_apply` 会让 COMMIT 等待到什么状态？这对只读查询的可见性意味着什么？
details.reference_answer: `remote_apply` 会让每次提交等待当前同步备库确认已经重放该事务；因此事务随后对备库上的用户查询可见。
details.model_answer:
BEGIN FINAL ANSWER
PostgreSQL’s `synchronous_commit=remote_apply` makes the primary wait for the synchronous standby to acknowledge that it has received and applied the commit record before reporting success to the client. This means the primary will not report a successful commit until the standby has both received the commit record and made the data visible to queries on the standby. [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
When the primary is waiting for the standby and the client sends a cancel signal (for example, by pressing Ctrl+C in `psql`), the primary may locally commit the transaction and report success to the client, but the standby has not yet acknowledged the commit. In this case the transaction is locally committed on the primary but not yet replicated to the standby. [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
This behavior is expected and is a known limitation of PostgreSQL’s synchronous replication architecture. There are no plans to change it, as it would require PostgreSQL to implement its own distributed transaction manager. [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
The behavior is documented in the PostgreSQL documentation and has been discussed in the pgsql-hackers and pgsql-general mailing lists. [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)

details.model_answer: SWE-bench Verified is a human-validated subset of the original SWE-bench dataset, consisting of 500 samples that evaluate AI models’ ability to solve real-world GitHub issues. The dataset was curated through a rigorous human annotation process involving 93 software developers. Each sample is reviewed by three separate annotators to ensure the issue description is well-specified, the unit tests are appropriate, and the sample is free of other major issues that could make evaluation unreliable. The evaluation workflow is as follows: the model is given access to a code repository and a description of an issue to be fixed. The model must then investigate and modify the repository to resolve the issue. Once the model has made its changes, the solution is evaluated by running unit tests on the modified repository. The tests are called `FAIL_TO_PASS` and `PASS_TO_PASS`. The `FAIL_TO_PASS` tests are required to pass after the model has made its changes, and the `PASS_TO_PASS` tests are used to verify that the model does not cause regressions. The benchmark has undergone several updates, including improvements to scaffolding, environments, and token limits. The latest version, v3, is available on Hugging Face.
